title: A serum-protein classifier fails to reproduce its early-infection discrimination in a second clinical cohort
summary: A random-forest model using four circulating proteins distinguished later invasive-aspergillosis cases from non-infected hematology controls in its derivation data, but the source reports that it failed to reproduce this performance in a second cohort. This negative retrospective validation is separate from the paper’s conventional differential-protein findings and does not establish a usable early diagnostic test.
ai_technology: Random forest classification of circulating-protein measurements
organization: University Hospitals Leuven; Radboud University Medical Center; Medical University of Graz

evidence.tested: The discovery study included 33 cases and two matched 33-person control groups. The RF used four selected proteins measured more than ten days before clinical diagnosis, and was then assessed in a separate cohort nominally comprising 20 cases and 20 non-infected controls. The source reports 87% derivation accuracy and 47% in the second cohort, explicitly concluding that the model did not replicate.
evidence.unknown: The main paper does not fully specify RF tuning, the person-versus-serum-sample denominator for these accuracy figures, uncertainty intervals or all handling of repeated longitudinal samples. Cohorts came from the same center and differed in immune-status/treatment characteristics. No significant differential proteins distinguished cases from infected controls after multiplicity correction. The failed classifier is not evidence of an infection-specific mechanism, actionable screening rule or patient benefit.
evidence.ai_role: A learned RF combined the four selected protein measurements into a case-classification rule. Its failure to transfer to a second observed clinical cohort is the represented clinical validation result; the separate IL-17C association was obtained through conventional differential analysis and is not attributed to AI.

source_review.scope: Read original clinical cohort/control and time-window definitions, RF construction and second-cohort model Results, conventional-marker analysis distinction and cohort/reference limitations. No biological operational protocol is represented or required. Original publisher February26 date verified. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.
